lv_s_max.source: network share of world compute at full mobilisation (a = 50%): incentives plus ideology; consumer/edge usable 0.3-2M H100e of ~29M DC stock plus joined DC capacity (r13a)

lv_E.source: governance wildcard: innovation efficiency per unit compute vs centralized, central 1 (0.5-3): OSS/open-weight record, no evidence of higher frontier R&D efficiency (r14b)

lv_spd.source: governance wildcard: decision speed vs a centralized/autocratic actor, 0.5 (0.2-1): DAO 7-day minimum cycle (Compound docs) vs executive decisions (r14b)

lv_M.source: relative amortization advantage on covered tasks vs centralized providers (who also cache/distil/reuse) (r14b)

lv_cmax.source: coverable ceiling of task volume (AEI bottom 80% of categories = 10.5-12.7% of use; 31% repeat queries; 44% routine jobs) (r14b)

lv_tau.source: coverage growth time constant, use-years (modelling assumption; Zipf task distribution) (r14b)

lv_lag_pre.source: network's own novel-task lag before any cut, months: open-weight lag 3.5 (1.1-5.3), consumer-GPU lag 6-12 (Epoch) (r14b)

lv_L27.source: lag per 10x compute gap under closure, months (derived from 8-month algorithmic halving, Ho et al. 2024) (r14b)

lv_p_oc.source: P(some open-weight releases continue after centralized providers cut frontier access) (strategic choice of a few firms/one state, m7)

lv_dlag_oc.source: extra lag (months) when only lower-tier open releases continue

lv_h_net.source: share of network activity that stops if participants withdraw (their hardware, review, keys): labour-like leverage under A6

lv_y_h.source: share of network value reaching human participants as income (rest: energy, chips)

lv_s_acc.source: share of network livelihoods that survive a state's deliberate strangulation of land/energy/food (m7: parallel economies depend on access)

lv_h0_dem.source: crackdown hazard/yr, small low-visibility network in a democracy (Christiania since 1971; WIR 90 years)

lv_h0_aut.source: crackdown hazard/yr, small network in an autocracy (Falun Gong pre-1999; China crypto escalation 2013/2017/2021)

lv_k.source: size elasticity of the hazard (crypto bans 23 -> 51 countries as market cap grew 5-10x, 2018-2021)

lv_thr_aut.source: autocracy threat threshold, share of activity (Falun Gong ~70M > CCP, banned July 1999)

lv_thr_dem.source: democracy threshold where the network erodes tax/monetary control (Worgl, Liberty Dollar, Tornado Cash)

lv_p_thr.source: P(suppression) once above the threshold (m7; crypto bans; Falun Gong)

lv_T_thr.source: years over which p_thr is realised above the threshold (Falun Gong ~3 months after Zhongnanhai; Worgl ~1 y; crypto bans years)

lv_eff.source: share of realised adoption removed by one crackdown (China mining 34% -> 0% -> 14-20% underground; Tornado Cash usage fell but did not stop) (m7 #26)

lv_rho0.source: recovery rate/yr after a crackdown at median governance speed (China Bitcoin mining back to ~half within ~1-2 y)

lv_R_gp.source: max hazard reduction from foreign public support, great power acting on a core interest (Hong Kong 2020, Tibet, Xinjiang, Kurdistan 2017)

lv_R_dep.source: same, repressor dependent on the supporters (Levitsky-Way linkage/leverage; South Africa, East Timor, Solidarity)

lv_sev.source: reduction of crackdown severity by foreign attention (Krain 2012; Hafner-Burton 2008 caveat)

lv_e.source: exponent on foreign publics' remaining leverage (structural inference)

lv_Ty.source: years to majority foreign favourability via culture (Hallyu 1997-2010s; Cold War cultural diplomacy)

lv_rev.source: favourability reversal after a hostile event, own public of the cracking-down state (Japan affinity to Korea 63% -> 39%; Pew US 64 -> 22)

lv_cut.source: effectiveness of an autocratic state cutting the cultural channel (China Hallyu ban after THAAD; Great Firewall)

lv_p_sc.source: P(self-governing enclaves are read as a sovereignty claim by the host state)

lv_p_ss.source: P(suppression | sovereignty claim within reach) (Rose Island 55 days; Kirkuk 21 days; Minerva; Catalonia)

lv_lag_ss.source: years from claim to suppression (Kirkuk 21 d, Rose Island 55 d, Falun Gong ~3 months)

lv_k_seed.source: A11 no-witness logic: rise of perceived revenge threat per 1% of the population living in self-sufficient enclaves (cap 10%)

lv_claw.source: benefit-reduction (claw-back) rate of state provision against network income: means-tested programmes withdraw 0.3 (SNAP) to 0.55 (UK Universal Credit) to 1.0 (SSI, unearned income) per unit of other income

lv_rho_cl.source: recovery rate/yr after a crackdown in a CLOSED autocratic bloc (regime controls energy, compute, land): Falun Gong inside China has not recovered since 1999; China's mining recovery relied on globally mobile hardware and capital

lv_kc.source: L1: network compute per unit of activity relative to the centralized economy (inference-heavy; the centralized side also spends 30-50% of compute on frontier training/R&D)

lv_eps_lab.source: L2: elasticity of frontier-lab capex to expected revenue (capex ~5-10x AI revenue, debt/growth-contingent finance: OpenAI ~$13B 2025 revenue vs ~$1.4T commitments; telecom capex -50-60% 2000-02)

lv_eps_hyp.source: L2: elasticity of cash-flow-funded capex (hyperscalers, industrial automation) to revenue relative to capital (Fazzari-Hubbard-Petersen 0.3-0.6; Meta 2022)

lv_lag_cx.source: L2: capex response lag, years (telecom bust, 2022 tech)

lv_g_eff.source: L2: log growth/yr of the input whose level capex sets: training compute 4-5x/yr (ln 1.4-1.6) if algorithmic progress scales with experiment compute, up to compute x algorithms ~13x/yr (ln 2.6) if it does not (Epoch; Ho et al. 2024)

lv_l4.source: L4: centralized revenue lost per unit withdrawing customer share when a substitute exists (Bud Light -25-30% peak, ~-40% persisting, AB InBev US revenue -13.5%; Montgomery; BDS ~0 without substitute)

lv_pers.source: L4: persistence of a withdrawal after 2 years (Bud Light; Chinese boycotts of Lotte/Hyundai)

lv_kpol.source: L4: political weight of customer leverage relative to labour leverage (revenue loss alone did not win Montgomery or apartheid: courts and elite defection were needed)

lv_xs.source: L7: export share of a bloc's revenue exposed to cross-bloc withdrawal (world exports ~29% of GDP)

lv_mv.source: L5: share of frontier talent willing to move (about half of OpenAI's safety team left in 2024; 97% letter as the solidarity ceiling)

lv_el5.source: L5: elasticity of the centralized capability rate to its top-talent share before R&D automation (OpenAI letter; Anthropic at the frontier ~2 years after the split; $1-100M packages)

lv_pcm.source: L6: P(crackdown takes the capture/regulate form | network share > 15%) (China 2020-23 subordinated platforms, ~$1T value lost; India demonetisation 86% of currency, government re-elected)

lv_kap.source: L6: depth of capture, share of the network's control/refusal capacity subordinated to the state

lv_eff_cap.source: L6: share of realised adoption lost in a capture (platforms kept operating in China after 2021)

lv_rcap_dem.source: L6: capture reversal rate/yr in a democracy (Prohibition repealed after 13 years; courts)

lv_rcap_aut.source: L6: capture reversal rate/yr in an autocracy (China eased in 2023 but kept golden shares)

lv_dm.source: L6: supply-chain multiplier of a full ban's direct cost (demonetisation PMI 54.5 -> 46.7)

lv_spd8.source: L8: speed multiplier on the organising part of a collective response (Egypt 18 days, Tunisia 28; OpenAI letter 3 days; IT Army 2 days; DAO fork 33 days; rulemaking 1-2 years)

lv_dur.source: L8: durability of digitally organised action (Tufekci 2017; Chenoweth 2020 post-2010 decline)

lv_forg.source: L8: organising share of a collective response's duration (the rest is courts, elections, institutions)

lv_rec9.source: L9: recruitment multiplier from legitimacy on recovery after a crackdown (nonviolent campaigns ~4x participants)

lv_bf.source: L9: net repression backfire on ban effectiveness, mean ~0 (Stephan & Chenoweth 2008 Table 3: regime violence no significant effect within nonviolent campaigns)

lv_defup.source: L9: defection uplift (RRR) on success, human-staffed share only (Stephan & Chenoweth 2008: 4.44 overall; nonviolence does not raise defection probability)

lv_pdoc.source: L9: P(defections occur) in a campaign (32% of successful violent, 52% of successful nonviolent campaigns)

lv_dnet.source: R3/C3: share of a repression order's execution that depends on capability the network supplies and the state cannot route around before the order runs (civilian logistics, energy, comms; the Reichsbahn and Rwanda's radio show civilian chains mattered; under A3 the coercive apparatus itself is state-owned automation and the state can requisition)

lv_tax.source: R3/C4: share of network activity inside the state's tax base (informal economy ~0, card/platform income ~0.8-1, crypto reporting rules phasing in)

lv_ccs.source: R3/C4-L1: compute and energy cost share of activity in an AI-heavy economy (today DC capex ~0.5% of world GDP; capex runs 5-10x AI revenue during the build-out); the network pays kc x ccs of its value for hardware, so y_h <= 1 - kc ccs

lv_psic.source: R3/L2: share of the network's hardware/energy spending that goes to centralized suppliers (TSMC, Nvidia, utilities)

lv_sub.source: R3/L4: share of participants' remaining spending on centralized goods that has a substitute or can be deferred (US CEX: housing 33%, transport 17%, food 13%, health 8% are hard to withdraw)

lv_avote.source: R3/L6: network share above which a democracy no longer bans it outright (participants as a voter bloc); P(ban | crackdown, democracy) x max(0, 1 - a / a_vote)

lv_kcost.source: R3/L6: weight of the anticipated self-inflicted output loss (eff x a x dm) on choosing capture/regulation over a ban: P(ban) x exp(-k_cost x loss) (China 2021 chose capture of platforms worth ~$1T; India's demonetisation shows large self-harm does happen)

lv_kphys.source: R3/closure: network share of the core physical chain relative to its overall share (fabs and mines are capital-concentrated; distributed solar and owner-operator logistics are not; security sector 0 under A3)

lv_gc.source: R3/L1: log growth/yr of the centralized compute stock over the period (2-3x/yr today, slowing)

lv_dep.source: R3/L1: depreciation of compute hardware/yr (4-6 year accounting lives)

lv_wlab.source: R3/L1: frontier-lab share of centralized compute (global sales, eps_lab); the rest is hyperscaler/enterprise compute funded from bloc revenue (eps_hyp)

lv_st.source: R3/L1: state-owned compute (A3 security automation, national labs) as a share of baseline centralized compute; exempt from revenue starvation

lv_mig.source: R3/L6: share of banned network activity that migrates back to centralized firms (the rest is lost output for a while)

lv_Tre.source: R3/L6: years for lost output after a ban to be re-absorbed (India demonetisation: ~1 year)

lv_dur3.source: R3/L8: success/durability factor of digitally organised action (nonviolent campaign success ~65% in the 1990s vs ~34% in the 2010s, Chenoweth 2020; Tufekci 2017): faster onset, less success, so the recovery multiplier is centred near 1

lv_pdoc3.source: R3/L9: unconditional P(security defections) across campaigns, derived from 52%/32% among successful campaigns, a 0.34-0.53 success base and fewer defections among failures (J-derived)
